key: tells you the real trend. Comparing with
name: ch11_run_rate_scoreboard_trend
alt: A stadium scoreboard where jumpy runs-per-over bars sit under a smooth five-over run-rate line, compared with the same stage of the last match.
scene: A cricket stadium at dusk seen from the stands, dominated by a giant electronic scoreboard on the right two-thirds of the frame. The scoreboard shows a simple bar chart of runs scored in each over: the bars jump wildly up and down, one very tall bar for an over with a six, then three tiny stubs for overs of dot balls, then a medium bar. Laid over the bars runs a thick, smooth amber line that rises gently, the average of the last five overs, clearly calmer than the jagged bars beneath it. A faint dashed grey line runs lower across the same board, showing the same stage of the previous match, with a small exclamation badge where today's smooth line pulls well above it. In the left foreground, a commentator in his fifties with a headset, a striped tie and reading glasses leans out of the commentary box and points his pen at the smooth line, calm and knowing, while a young fan beside the box in a blue jersey stares at the tallest bar and cheers wildly, waving a flag. Floodlight towers glow behind, a few seagulls circle. The contrast between the excited fan reacting to one over and the calm commentator reading the trend carries the idea. Labels: "THIS OVER" above the jagged bars, and "LAST 5 OVERS" beside the smooth amber line.

key: Aadhaar address is a materialized view
name: ch11_id_address_ledger_vs_hourly_board
alt: A records clerk's ID card reflects a thick ledger of every address change ever filed, while a wall board counts only this hour's change requests.
scene: The inside of a government citizen-service centre, framed as a split scene across one long room. On the left, a records clerk in his forties with a moustache, half-sleeve shirt and spectacles sits behind a counter with a very thick bound ledger, its pages stuffed with years of address-change slips sticking out of the edges, the oldest yellowed. From the ledger, a curved arrow leads up to a large national ID card displayed on a stand, showing a small portrait and one neat house icon for the latest address only; small faded house icons trail behind it like a history of older homes, folded into the ledger. On the right side of the room, a wall-mounted board shows a short bar chart of address-change requests per hour, and right next to it hangs a large hourglass marked for one hour. A young woman clerk in a cotton salwar kameez with a dupatta drops today's fresh slips from a small wire tray into a counting box under the board, ignoring the old ledger entirely. A queue of three citizens with folders waits at the counter. Ceiling fans, steel cupboards, a wall clock and afternoon light through barred windows. The point is visible at a glance: the card depends on every slip ever filed, the board only on the last hour's slips. Labels: "ALL HISTORY" above the thick ledger, and "LAST HOUR" above the hourly board.

key: Actors are colleagues phoning each other
name: ch11_office_phone_tag_vs_assembly_line
alt: Two colleagues phone requests back and forth with nothing written down, beside a one-way factory assembly line where every station logs its output.
scene: A split-panel illustration divided by a thin vertical line. LEFT panel: an open-plan office with two colleagues at facing desks, a woman in her thirties in a teal kurta and a young man in a checked shirt, both holding desk phones to their ears. Curved arrows loop back and forth between them in both directions, with small speech bubbles, one holding a question mark and one holding a tick, the answer coming back to the asker. On each desk lies a notepad that is completely blank, a pen resting on it unused, showing nothing is recorded. A third colleague in the background also has a phone cord stretching across the aisle, adding another loop. RIGHT panel: a bright factory floor with a long conveyor belt running strictly left to right through three work stations, each with a worker in overalls and a cap fitting a part to a box. Beside each station hangs a clipboard logbook full of ticked lines, one per part that passed. At the far left end of the belt, a supervisor in a hard hat lifts a crate of parts back onto the belt just before the middle station, a curved arrow showing the batch being re-run through that same station, which has not changed. Only one-way arrows on the belt. Even daylight from high factory windows. Labels: "ACTORS" at the top of the left panel, and "STREAM PIPELINE" at the top of the right panel.

name: ch11_cricket_window_kinds
alt: Four cricket strips showing balls boxed into separate overs, overlapping five-over brackets, a stopwatch between two boundaries, and a batter's innings ending at a wicket.
scene: A wide illustration made of four horizontal strips stacked from top to bottom, all drawn on a long green cricket-ground band with a timeline running left to right. Top strip: a row of red cricket balls grouped into neat boxes of six, every ball sitting in exactly one box, the boxes touching edge to edge with no overlap. Second strip: the same balls, but long translucent amber brackets each covering five overs, each bracket shifted one over to the right of the one before, so they overlap like roof tiles, a small refresh arrow at the end of each. Third strip: a scattered line of balls with two of them glowing as boundaries, a large stopwatch hovering between them with a bracket measuring the gap, no boxes at all, showing there are no fixed edges. Bottom strip: a batter in white with a helmet and pads stands at the left end of a long bar that grows as he keeps scoring; at the right end the stumps are knocked over with bails flying, and after that the bar stops and a quiet empty stretch of ground follows, marked by a little sleeping moon to show silence. A scoreboard and floodlights appear faintly in the background, and soft afternoon sunlight falls across the field. The four strips stay clean and diagrammatic so the four ways of cutting time can be compared at a glance. Labels: "TUMBLING" beside the top strip, "HOPPING" beside the second strip, and "SESSION" beside the bottom strip.

name: ch11_wedding_planner_rsvp_matching
alt: A wedding planner matches reply cards trickling in to invitation stubs sent over weeks, using an address book that keeps changing, while a postman keeps arriving.
scene: A wedding planner's small office a few weeks before a wedding, seen from the front. At the centre a woman planner in her thirties, in a bright printed saree with a pencil tucked in her bun, sits at a desk with two wire trays. The left tray holds a long fanned-out stack of invitation stubs, each marked with a small calendar page showing different weeks they were posted. The right tray holds reply cards with small tick or cross marks. With a red thread she ties one reply card to its matching invitation stub, a few earlier pairs already tied together on the desk. Between the trays lies a thick open address book, with an eraser, a sticky note and a pencil showing an address being corrected right now. At the door on the right, a postman in khaki with a satchel hands over yet another reply card, and through the window a line of more postmen and cyclists stretches down the road with no end in sight. On the wall behind her, a poster of a plan that reads like a neat sorted list is crossed out with a big red cross. Strings of marigold and a wedding card sample on a pin board add warmth. Morning light. The picture should feel calm but never finished. Labels: "TWO STREAMS" above the two trays, and "TABLE" beside the address book.
